title: Northstar tether: consolidated workspace quick-jump & cost-lens IA redesign
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Rework the Console information architecture to make workspace switching, route discovery, and cost lenses discoverable and consistent across personas (engineer, platform admin, finance reviewer). This ticket surfaces a prototype for a tethered quick-jump rail (the "Northstar Tether") that lives in a collapsed sidebar state and expands into a contextual rail. It also defines how the cost-lens and rollout controls surface in that flow so customers can get to per-route cost and rollout toggles in 1–2 interactions. Outcomes: reduced time-to-task for workspace switch, clearer route ownership, and an unobtrusive cost-first view for billing-minded users.
background: Current console navigation mixes workspace switching, model/route-level dashboards, and rollout controls across top nav, left rail, and ad-hoc modal patterns. Research (support tickets + usability sessions) shows finance users get lost finding per-route cost reports; platform teams miss rollout toggles during on-call. Past design attempts focused on a large workspace switcher modal; that solution increased context switching time. This design explores a persistent, compact rail that exposes high-frequency actions and a cost micro-dashboard inline.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prototype demonstrates workspace switch in <=2 interactions from any page. 2) Cost lens opens inline and displays tokens/day, avg latency, and 3-month spend trend for the selected route. 3) Rollout toggle (canary/A-B) visible within rail with clear status and CTA to open release manager. 4) Usability benchmark: 80% of test participants complete task of 'find route cost and toggle canary' within 45s. 5) Implementation-ready handoff with annotated Figma frames and component spec.
decisions: Keep primary left rail collapsed by default for dense dashboards; reveal Northstar tether as a compact handle.
Expose top-3 actions in the tether: Workspace Switch, Route Cost, Rollout Controls.
Inline cost-lens is read-only; links out to a full cost dashboard for deep analysis.
Rollout actions in rail show status and one-click fallback; full changes require Console release manager.
Use existing role-aware filtering so finance sees cost-first items while engineers see recent routes and traces.
tradeoffs: Risk of cluttering collapsed rail vs. improved discovery — mitigated with progressive disclosure and persona-aware defaults.
Inline cost numbers may be noisy for routes with spiky traffic — chosen to show rolling averages and percentile metrics to reduce noise.
Rollout quick-action reduces time to change but increases potential accidental toggles — we introduce confirmation and rewind affordances.
review_comments: PM (Noah Rivera): Ensure the cost lens includes 3-month trend and attribution by model variant.
Eng (Priya Kapoor): Need backend contract for cost micro-API; latency target <200ms for tether open.
Security (Marco Diaz): Confirm RBAC for rollout toggles; disallow canary edits for billing-only roles.
Design (Maya Ortiz): Suggest micro-animations for tether expand/collapse to preserve mental model.
Accessibility (Hana Lee): Verify keyboard-only navigation and screen reader announcements for rail state.
implementation_notes: Front-end will reuse SideRail component v2. Add new compact-tether variant and cost-micro API integration. Backend work requires API: GET /routes/{id}/micro_cost and POST /routes/{id}/rollout_action with audit logging. Include feature flag console_northstar_tether for staged rollout.
risks: Backend cost aggregation may be slow for large orgs; add caching and pre-aggregation for top routes.
Feature discoverability for deeply nested routes — mitigate with telemetry and contextual nudges.
Potential duplication with existing workspace modal — plan to deprecate modal after 2-week A/B.
metrics: Time to task: workspace switch (baseline 9s) target <4s
Route cost discovery rate: increase from 22% to 65% in 6 weeks
Rollout error rate: maintain <=0.5% after quick-action introduction
Adoption: >=30% of active orgs using tether within first month behind flag
